cards.title: Drug Model Predictive Performance Evaluation
cards.claim: The predictive performance of the specific drug model must be evaluated by comparing simulated plasma concentration-time data against observed individual data from representative in vivo studies. This evaluation should cover different dose levels, single/repeated administration, and relevant populations. Visual predictive plots comparing central trends and variability (5th/95th percentiles) are required. The evaluation must focus on the parts of the model central to the intended purpose (e.g., Cmax/t1/2 for intestinal vs. hepatic metabolism).
conditions: Required before using the model to simulate novel situations (e.g., DDIs, alternate populations).
Simulations should be performed in the population of interest for a large number of individuals (>100 recommended).
Acceptance criteria for prediction closeness depend on regulatory impact and concentration-effect relationships.
required_inputs: Observed individual PK data from representative studies.
Statistical metrics (geometric mean, SD, range) and visual plots (linear and semi-log).
Justification for any discrepancies between simulated and observed data.
limitations: Does not prescribe a universal numerical threshold for 'good' prediction; acceptance is context-dependent.
Excerpts do not include the full text of Appendix 2 examples, limiting specific scenario details beyond the general principles.
cards.downstream_use: Provides the standard for validating that a human simulation model is fit for purpose before generating prospective exposure scenarios. Defines the evidence needed to trust simulated PK parameters.

note: Method/reference scope retained; source identity is available in original evidence.
